program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s binding is ambiguous: the source shows a small disc in a case near the center, while the edited image shows two white discs, including one near the dark object. The traces repeatedly call the DVD white but do not establish which edited disc corresponds to the source DVD or whether the dark object is relevant; their high confidence and repetition do not resolve that identity. Tighten the target binding to the source disc using its location/context and require comparison of that same object across snapshots. Preserve the requested-color criterion, but distinguish complete change from partial progress and absent change based on visible evidence; if correspondence cannot be established, return unresolved rather than treating any white disc as proof of completion. The reference label alone is not atomic ground truth. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
